Q: Is the torch.fx traced graph topologically sorted? A:

Yes. The order of nodes in a torch.fx Graph is always a valid topological sort.

James Reed, the original creator and lead maintainer of torch.fx has stated this :

"Topological order is a hard invariant of torch.fx Graph. It is always true. You never need to toposort an fx graph. If you ever find a graph that is not topologically sorted, that is a bug in PyTorch, and you should report it."

Q: Copying a file with robocopy (long name and path, and many spaces) - Missing argument A:

It's worth heeding Theo's advice: enclosing your file names that contain spaces and other special characters either in single quotes ('...', for verbatim values) or double quotes ("...", if you need string interpolation) is the simplest solution.[1]

While escaping characters individually with `, without enclosing quoting does work, it's visually less obvious and, as in your case, it is easy to miss characters that need escaping:

In PowerShell ,, (, and ) are also metacharacters that require escaping in order to be interpreted verbatim, and you neglected to escape them.

Therefore, escape as follows, using Write-Output as an example command to demonstrate that the names are parsed correctly:

PS> Write-Output D:\Enciclopedia` mia\Tutorial` FATTI` DA` ME\Internet\Google\Limitare` permessi` di` alcune` celle` o` colonne` o` righe` in` Google` Sheets C:\Users\Raffaele\Desktop` Protect`,` hide`,` and` edit` sheets` -` Computer` `(Proteggere`,` limitare` permessi` di` alcune` celle` o` colonne` o` righe` in` Google` Sheets`)` -` Docs` Editors` Help.pdf

D:\Enciclopedia mia\Tutorial FATTI DA ME\Internet\Google\Limitare permessi di alcune celle o colonne o righe in Google Sheets
C:\Users\Raffaele\Desktop Protect, hide, and edit sheets - Computer (Proteggere, limitare permessi di alcune celle o colonne o righe in Google Sheets) - Docs Editors Help.pdf

List of metacharacters that require individual escaping in unquoted command arguments:

# See below for additional chars. that SITUATIONALLY require escaping.
<space> ' " ` , ; ( ) { } | & < > @ #

Note:

  • Of these, < > @ # are only special at the start of an argument.

  • If you want a $ to be treated verbatim rather than refer to a variable or subexpression, you must escape it too.

  • Situationally, escaping may be required for additional characters:

    • . (dot) requires escaping if the argument would otherwise syntactically be interpreted as accessing a variable (value's) property (e.g., Write-Output $env:computername.csv outputs nothing - see this answer).

    • When calling external (native) programs, unquoted ~ (in PowerShell (Core) 7 on Unix-like platforms and on Windows in v7.6+) and * / ? (on Unix-like platforms only) trigger tilde expansion (resolving ~ to the full path of the user's home directory) and pathname expansion (globbing), respectively.
      Unexpectedly, as of PowerShell 7.6.0, individual `-escaping of these characters does not work (only using '...' or "..." quoting does): see GitHub issue #27116.

  • For a complete overview of how unquoted command arguments are parsed in PowerShell, see this answer.

[1] See the bottom section of this answer for an overview of PowerShell string literals in general, and this answer for the rules of string interpolation in so-called expandable strings ("..."), specifically.

Q: How to unescape HTML entities in python A:

Its easier to use a regex to match the name or code number, then do a replacement:
(?i)&(?:([a-z]+)|\#(?:([0-9]+)|x([0-9a-f]+))); https://regex101.com/r/nxOU63/1

I'll write up a sample Python using a gsub callback to do the replacement.. shortly.
Note this is only for Character Entity References in HTML not Parameter Entities (DTDs)

(?i)                          # Case insensitive
&                             # Ampersand
(?:
  ( [a-z]+ )                    # (1), Name hash lookup
|                              # or,
  \#                            # Numeric
  (?:
    ( [0-9]+ )                    # (2), Decimal code
  | x 
    ( [0-9a-f]+ )                 # (3), Hexidecimal code
  )
)
;

Q: css with crystal reports A:

You would have to use the formatter provided by the crystal report application. The reason why you can't find a HTML file to format with CSS is because crystal reports dynamically creates the HTML file, meaning you'll never see that file. If you want to customize yourself, create your on HTML template and then style it with CSS.

Q: kubectl returns "Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate is valid for..." A:

Just as a workaround, on the client host create an SSH tunnel to the remote host (where Minikube is running). Then simply use https://127.0.0.1:<APISERVER_PORT> in the Kubeconfig.

The certificate will be valid because 127.0.0.1 is in SAN of the default certificate.

This approach worked for me.
